study type: Secondary analysis of a cluster-randomised controlled trial
exposure: newborns moved slowly immediately after birth
cohort: Mothers (n=3594) participating in a cluster-randomised controlled trial in rural northwest Bangladesh.
finding: The prevalence of late initiation of breastfeeding (LIBF) was 18.5%, and it was significantly associated with assisted vaginal delivery, caesarean section, maternal health problems during childbirth, preterm newborns, newborns who moved slowly immediately after birth, and sick newborns.
mod_finding: Assisted vaginal delivery (AOR 2.17) and caesarean section (AOR 9.67) were significantly associated with late initiation of breastfeeding.
cross-section timing: Within the first 72 hours of delivery
